Unity compliance audit and remediation on 2026-09-20 against the current UMass Unity documentation. Two violations were found in this session's own work and corrected. First, the embedding Conda environment was built with nohup on a login node. Unity states that login-node work can make the cluster sluggish for the entire user base, that CPU and memory there are deliberately limited, and that disruptive login-node processes may be terminated without notice, directing users to salloc and sbatch instead. The build also failed on its own terms with 'nothing provides __cuda', because conda detects the __cuda virtual package only where a GPU is present, so a CUDA pytorch build cannot be solved on a login node at all; no environment was created and nothing was left running. Second, that ad-hoc command bypassed the project's existing hpc/unity/disjointness-env.sbatch pattern and therefore did not export CONDA_PKGS_DIRS, so the package cache defaulted to the 100 GB home directory, where ~/.conda already stands at 27 GB. Remediation: added hpc/unity/embeddings-env.sbatch following the established pattern with a GPU request so __cuda resolves, CONDA_PKGS_DIRS redirected into the work allocation, spec-hash stamping, and recorded torch, CUDA, transformers, and device provenance. Verified against the documentation and corrected in docs/UNITY_HPC.md: cpu, gpu, cpu-preempt and gpu-preempt all allow up to 14 days with a 1-hour default so --time must always be set explicitly, --qos=long is required to reach 14 days, a preempt-partition job can be killed after two hours, and valid GPU constraints are vram8 through vram102, sm_52 through sm_90, and model names such as a100, a100-80g, l40s, a16 and gh200. The existing 36-hour cpu job and the vram40 canary constraint were both confirmed valid. Added four executable compliance guards in tests/test_unity_disjointness_scripts.py: every Conda environment job must redirect the package cache off home, the GPU environment build must request a GPU, every preempt-partition job must stay within the two-hour kill window, and every declared GPU constraint must be a valid Unity constraint name. External exclusion threshold amendment 003 adopted 2026-09-21 (docs/EXTERNAL_THRESHOLD_AMENDMENT.md), partly superseding amendment 002. The rule removing an external isolate from the locked evaluation changes from the near-neighbour threshold (ANI at least 99.9, minimum reciprocal aligned fraction at least 0.9) to the putative-duplicate threshold (ANI at least 99.99, minimum reciprocal aligned fraction at least 0.95). Both values were already frozen in disjointness_contract.json, so no new threshold is introduced; only which prespecified rule governs exclusion changes. Rationale: the NEAR_NEIGHBOR class in comparison 63772662 spans ANI 99.90 to 100.00 with median 99.93 and 90th percentile 99.97, which for E. coli is ordinary similarity within a sequence type or clonal complex and indicates shared lineage rather than a shared isolate. Using it as the exclusion rule removed lineage membership rather than leakage, discarding the globally disseminated lineages that cause most human infection, silently converting the question from external validation into unseen-lineage prediction, and costing the power needed for the primary endpoint. Resulting structure, computed by the new executable rule and not by prose: external-locked 1,888 isolates of which 1,555 carry all three target MICs, external-excluded 1,271 putative genomic duplicates, and a nested lineage-novel stratum of 536 isolates with no collision of any class, of which 454 carry all three MICs. Membership artifact SHA-256 b4c6baf7479c5e109fdaa9b60ca9d09eb9014c24b27f9efaf1acdff2d39432e3. A confound was tested and dismissed: collision-free isolates are not merely fragmented assemblies, since median contigs are 188 versus 191, median coverage 53 versus 52, and median total bases 5,121,504 versus 5,140,678 against the colliding set. The headline external analysis becomes performance as a function of genomic distance to the training set, with the lineage-novel stratum as the most distant band, which uses the disjointness computation as a covariate rather than only as a filter. evidence.detail: Phenotype-free foundation-model infrastructure opened 2026-09-20 (docs/FOUNDATION_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md v0.1). The phase stays pending: this is preparation only and no exit criterion is met. Work started ahead of the locked baselines because embedding extraction consumes assemblies only and reads no MIC, category, split, or external membership, so it passes and skips no gate; the protocol states that computing a representation is not crediting a model and that no embedding may be evaluated against phenotype until rungs 1-4 are locked. Model selection records Evo 1 8k base as primary candidate for prokaryote-weighted pretraining and operon-scale context, the 131k variant as a long-context option, and DNABERT-2 only as a short-context comparator. A pretraining-overlap audit is specified as a hard gate: the development cohort is 10,334 public NCBI assemblies and Evo 1's OpenGenome corpus draws on GTDB and IMG prokaryotic genomes, so zero overlap is untenable. The audit must record checkpoint revision and training cutoff, count cohort assemblies released before that cutoff as candidate memorization sources, report a quantified residual risk rather than a clearance, and prefer lineage-holdout and genomically disjoint external comparisons over the more contaminated development folds. Windowing and aggregation are prespecified before extraction: non-overlapping native-context windows that never span a contig boundary, trailing windows below a minimum length dropped rather than padded, both strands embedded and averaged with the choice recorded, mean pooling as default, and layer fixed before extraction. Unity GPU preflight 64634160 completed 0:0 recording NVIDIA A16, compute capability 8.6, 15,356 MiB VRAM, driver 595.71.05 on gpu049; that satisfies the portable sm_70 and vram16 minimum but is insufficient for a 7B-parameter checkpoint, so the canary requests vram40. Implemented scripts/extract_genome_embeddings.py with an injected encoder so windowing, strand, and pooling are testable without a GPU or weights, a plan subcommand that refuses an unpinned model revision and records a sealed scientific boundary, and per-assembly window accounting including ambiguous-base counts. Added workflow/envs/embeddings.yaml and hpc/unity/embeddings-canary.sbatch, bounded to one GPU on gpu-preempt for 90 minutes, failing closed without a pinned model id and revision, keeping the HuggingFace cache inside the allocation rather than the 100 GB home directory, and refusing to overwrite an existing result. The embedding conda environment is still solving, no checkpoint has been downloaded, no canary has run, and no embedding exists. No model, phenotype, clinical, or causal claim is added.

Discovered on Unity: conda environments evo2 (evo2 0.5.5, flash-attn 2.8.0.post2, torch 2.7.1), evo2_1b (evo2 0.5.5 with vortex, torch 2.11.0+cu130), evo2_20b and evo2_20b_py311, plus a complete prior study in evo2_project that embeds RpoB DNA with Evo2, mean-pools over tokens, and compares against 3-mer, 4-mer, 6-mer, GC and length baselines using Pearson and Spearman correlation against phylogenetic distance. Two environment defects were diagnosed and one fixed. First, import evo2 failed with ldconfig -p grep libnvrtc returning non-zero: transformer_engine._load_nvrtc globs CUDA_HOME first and otherwise falls back to ldconfig, where check_output raises when grep matches nothing, so the LD_LIBRARY_PATH fallback is unreachable; Unity supplies CUDA through modules that set LD_LIBRARY_PATH without populating the ldconfig cache, and ldconfig -p grep -c libnvrtc returned 0 even with cuda/12.6 loaded. Verified fix in job 64663130: export CUDA_HOME to the environment's site-packages/nvidia, whose bundled libnvrtc.so.12 satisfies the glob; import then succeeds with CUDA available. This was confirmed not to be caused by the earlier package-cache cleanup, because the failing probe reads the system ld.so.cache, torch still imports, and the evo2, flash_attn and torch package directories remain present. Second, transformer_engine reports flash-attn 2.8.0.post2 above its supported ceiling of 2.7.4.post1; this remains an open warning and the observed version is now recorded with every run. The extraction layer is prespecified from the independent RpoB phylogeny sweep, which contains no AMR phenotype and therefore leaks nothing: archaea cosine Pearson r is 0.433 at blocks.6.mlp.l3, 0.421 at blocks.17, 0.397 at blocks.12, 0.108 at blocks.21 and 0.045 at blocks.23, so signal concentrates in early-to-mid blocks and collapses in deep ones. blocks.6.mlp.l3 is the prespecified primary layer with blocks.17.mlp.l3 as the single declared alternative. Absolute correlations near 0.43 on a phylogeny task are recorded as a caution that these representations are not obviously strong. SCOPE LIMIT: this canary exercised only the plan subcommand. It validated the environment, the CUDA_HOME fix, provenance capture and assembly enumeration. It did not load Evo 2 weights, did not run inference, and produced no embedding. Peak VRAM, throughput and reverse-complement consistency remain unmeasured. The installed evo2 0.5.5 package supports evo2_1b_base, evo2_7b, evo2_7b_base, evo2_20b, evo2_40b and evo2_40b_base. A second allocation directory rushath_umass_edu holds an unrelated Apptainer line of work with an empty hf_cache and no checkpoints. A byte-identical duplicate of evo2_7b in the home quota was removed by job 64668609 after verifying the work copy matched at 13,766,621,200 bytes with no incomplete blobs, reducing home .cache from 28 GB to 15 GB; a first attempt failed closed because sbatch --wrap executes under dash where set -o pipefail is invalid, and nothing was deleted. Hardware: gh200 was rejected because those nodes are aarch64 Grace Hopper on the arm-gpu partition and the existing x86_64 conda stack, including compiled flash-attn, cannot run there; a guard test now forbids any job targeting gh200 or arm-gpu. h200_nvl is x86_64 with 143 GB VRAM and sm_90, so the canary now requests vram143 with 128 GB host memory for the 20B. Live cluster features were read directly because the published constraint list is stale: it omits h100, h200, h200_nvl, vram143, sm_87 and sm_120, and the compliance test's valid set was corrected accordingly. SCIENTIFIC CORRECTION: the previous evidence entry justified prespecifying blocks.6.mlp.l3 as primary because it maximised RpoB phylogenetic correlation. That rationale is withdrawn. The RpoB task measures whether embeddings preserve evolutionary distance, that is whether they encode lineage, and lineage is the confounder this study exists to control rather than the target; a layer chosen to maximise phylogenetic signal may be the layer that best encodes population structure. The transfer is further weakened by scale, since RpoB is a single 4 kb conserved gene while the unit here is a 5 Mb draft assembly, and by evolutionary dynamics, since AMR determinants are frequently horizontally acquired accessory sequence while RpoB is a core gene under purifying selection, and the best correlation is a modest 0.43. The sweep is retained only as evidence that deep layers are degenerate, since r falls from 0.433 at blocks.6 to 0.108 at blocks.21 and 0.045 at blocks.23, consistent with a published stability boundary in deeper layers. Revised rule: the candidate set is blocks.6, blocks.12 and blocks.17 mlp.l3, all three extracted, with selection among them performed inside training folds on development data only and never on the external set or the phylogeny score. Phylogenetic structure in the chosen embedding is retained as a diagnostic warning sign for out-of-distribution behaviour rather than as a quality objective. Verification: 163 local tests pass including a new architecture guard. No embedding has been produced and no model, phenotype, clinical or causal claim is added.

Foundation-model protocol revision 0.2 adopted by the decision owner on 2026-09-27 (docs/FOUNDATION_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md): Evo 2 embeds resistance-relevant units instead of whole genomes. Units: 12 K-12 MG1655 chromosomal loci with 300 bp upstream (gyrA, gyrB, parC, parE, marR, acrR, soxR, ampC, ompF, ompC, ompR, envZ), located by blastn at >= 80 percent identity over >= 90 percent of the unit, else missing; and every complete AMRFinderPlus acquired gene with 500 bp flanks. Panel reference GCF_000005845.2 built by job 64966441 (unit lengths 735 to 2,928 bp; gyrA 2,928 = 2,628 + 300). Extraction array 64966442 (67 tasks) and collection 64966443 submitted on cohort 64948707. scripts/embed_resistance_units.py embeds deduplicated units on both strands with candidate layers blocks.6/12/17 mlp.l3 in one pass, averages strands, records reverse-complement cosine, and writes hash-checked resumable shards; hpc/unity/embeddings-units.sbatch runs on gpu-preempt H200 NVL (the only partition with H200) in under-2-hour resumable tasks, reading the existing Evo 2 weights offline. No phenotype read by any embedding step.

Pre-registration, decision owner 2026-09-28 (commit a34bfca, 14:44 UTC), before any all-sources Evo 2 result or external MIC was read: (1) Evo 2 credit rule in docs/FOUNDATION_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md: credited per antibiotic only if AMR+Evo 2 beats AMR alone for both learners in human-clinical development nested CV with paired lineage-bootstrap intervals excluding zero, and on the locked external evaluation, with the overlap audit reported; all-sources results cannot create credit. At adoption only gentamicin met the development condition (ridge +0.027 [+0.010, +0.038]; XGBoost +0.024 [+0.001, +0.043]). (2) MIC_EVALUATION_SPEC addendum A: every model reported by reference class with the right-censored under-call rate (MIC analogue of a very major error; clinical devices must stay below about 1.5 percent). Human-clinical development diagnostics (job 64983779 outputs, development only): AMRFinderPlus models under-call right-censored rows 3.7 to 4.2 percent (ciprofloxacin), 10.8 to 16.8 percent (ceftriaxone), 14.0 to 18.7 percent (gentamicin), so no model is clinically usable; the no-genome constant scores 1.000 on left-censored and 0.000 on right-censored rows. Evo 2-only XGBoost failed on ciprofloxacin only in outer fold 1, which holds the SLV:ST131 group (EA 0.254 on 934 ST131 rows versus 0.902 for AMRFinderPlus XGBoost on the same rows; other folds 0.896 to 0.922): an embedding tree model fails when the dominant lineage is unseen; ridge on Evo 2 features did not (ST131 0.869). Pretraining overlap: OpenGenome2 (arcinstitute/opengenome2) uses one representative genome per GTDB species (releases 214.1 and 220; the species_metadata.csv of 28,177 species lists only the release-220 additions and contains no Escherichia) plus IMG/PR plasmids, IMG/VR phages and metagenomes; the E. coli representative GCF_003697165.2 is not among the 13,493 cohort genome requests. Plasmid audit job 64994989 submitted (IMG/PR blastn of every unique acquired unit). Evaluator reference-class reporting, ablation feature sets (amr+evo2_panel, amr+evo2_acquired) and the audit are implemented with tests; 391 local tests pass.

Pretraining-overlap audit job 64994989 COMPLETE (5m03s; results/genomics/pretraining-overlap/64994989/overlap.json with artifact hashes). Chromosomes: OpenGenome2 represents E. coli by the single GTDB species representative GCF_003697165.2, which is not among the cohort genomes. Plasmids: of 22,767 unique acquired units searched against the OpenGenome2 IMG/PR set Evo 2 was trained on, 14,482 (64 percent) have a near-identical copy (identity >= 99 percent over >= 95 percent of the unit), 5,013 a close copy (>= 90 over >= 80) and 3,272 none; over isolate-unit rows 75,279 near-identical, 25,392 close, 25,610 not found. Common mobile determinants are near-identical almost always (sul1 4,703 of 4,931 rows, sul2 5,202 of 5,460, tet(A) 5,196 of 5,355, dfrA17 2,755 of 2,832, mph(A) 3,119 of 3,171, blaTEM-1 3,362 of 5,075). Not-found rows are dominated by intrinsic chromosomal genes that AMRFinderPlus reports as Subtype AMR (acrF 12,948, emrD 9,010), which are near-universal and therefore mostly lineage markers inside the acquired-unit mean embedding; the ablation must be read with this in mind. Overlap cannot leak MIC labels (Evo 2 saw no phenotype); it establishes that most acquired determinants were in-distribution for the model.

Evo 2 model round 64983779 COMPLETE (9h38m, checksums verified; embeddings 64983760: 64 shards, 4 H100 tasks of about 54 min, about 3.6 GPU-hours). Ridge AMR predictions reproduced round 2 exactly. AMR+Evo 2 minus AMR, paired lineage bootstrap. Human clinical: ceftriaxone ridge +0.009 [+0.002, +0.019], XGBoost -0.015 [-0.020, -0.007]; ciprofloxacin -0.003 [-0.013, +0.007], -0.005 [-0.017, +0.003]; gentamicin +0.027 [+0.010, +0.038], +0.024 [+0.001, +0.043] (credit condition 1 met for gentamicin only). All sources (sensitivity, cannot create credit): ceftriaxone +0.003 [-0.002, +0.008], -0.021 [-0.030, -0.012]; ciprofloxacin +0.011 [+0.002, +0.018], +0.001 [-0.004, +0.006]; gentamicin +0.005 [-0.002, +0.011], +0.003 [-0.005, +0.011]; the human-clinical gentamicin gain does not appear with 2.8 times more training data. Evo 2 alone trails AMRFinderPlus by 0.3 to 7.2 points (human clinical ridge: ceftriaxone -0.022, ciprofloxacin -0.028, gentamicin -0.003) except the XGBoost ciprofloxacin ST131-fold collapse. Defect found: the run logged 14 RuntimeWarnings (overflow in exp, invalid matmul/reduce) in ridge fits with Evo 2 features only (round 2 had none): unbounded, the L-BFGS line search could push log sigma far enough to overflow. Fixed by bounding sigma to [0.05, 64] log2 units and recording per-fold optimiser convergence, with a regression test. Rerun 65006995 (ridge, amr/amr+evo2/evo2, both populations, fixed optimiser) and ablation 65006996 (human clinical, ridge and XGBoost, amr+evo2_panel and amr+evo2_acquired) submitted; both the original and the rerun will be reported.

Rerun 65006995 (bounded optimiser, human-clinical part complete, zero RuntimeWarnings) reproduces round 64983779: AMR+Evo 2 minus AMR ridge, human clinical, ceftriaxone +0.009 [+0.002, +0.018], ciprofloxacin -0.003 [-0.013, +0.007], gentamicin +0.027 [+0.010, +0.038]; 20 of 1,275 fits flagged not converged (1.6 percent) and recorded; Evo 2 alone unchanged (-0.022, -0.028, -0.003). The optimiser defect did not affect conclusions. Ablation 65006996 COMPLETE (1h31m, checksums verified, zero warnings, all 3,420 ridge fits converged), human clinical, gain over AMR alone: gentamicin from acquired-unit embeddings ridge +0.031 [+0.017, +0.039], XGBoost +0.024 [+0.004, +0.039]; from chromosomal-panel embeddings +0.007 [-0.003, +0.015] and +0.010 [-0.025, +0.042] (not distinguishable). Panel embeddings slightly hurt ciprofloxacin (ridge -0.006 [-0.015, -0.002], XGBoost -0.020 [-0.029, -0.012]). Gentamicin right-censored under-call falls from 0.166 (AMR ridge) to 0.121 with acquired-unit embeddings. Interpretation, not a claim: the gentamicin signal lies in Evo 2 representations of acquired determinants and their 500 bp flanks (allele variant and promoter/integron/transposon context beyond AMRFinderPlus presence), consistent with acquired aac(3)/ant(2'') mechanisms; a plasmid-backbone or source-batch explanation cannot be excluded in development and is tested by the single-method external set. Development only; no external MIC read.

Diagnosis of the human-clinical gentamicin Evo 2 gain (development only; ablation 65006996, ridge AMR versus AMR + acquired-unit Evo 2). The rare-variant hypothesis is rejected: all 23 resistant rows rescued by Evo 2 carry common determinants (aac(3)-IId 246 isolates, aac(3)-IIe 205; rare determinants occur in only 3 resistant isolates, none rescued). Net gain is +83 rows on exact references and +21 on right-censored, 0 on left-censored; among exact rows it is +89 for isolates with no gentamicin determinant (EA 0.325 to 0.546, references mostly 1 to 2 mg/L) and -6 for carriers. 106 of 109 fixed no-determinant exact rows and 22 of 23 fixed resistant rows come from one BioProject, PRJNA1297298 (University of Liverpool, 762 clinical isolates 'selected to provide a broad range of minimum inhibitory concentration phenotypes for machine learning'), which supplies 14.9 percent of human-clinical gentamicin rows. Excluding that project, EA is 0.965 for both models: the Evo 2 gentamicin gain is entirely source-specific. Interpretation: Evo 2 acquired-unit features let the model recognise isolates from one phenotype-enriched collection whose laboratory reports susceptible gentamicin MICs as exact 1 to 2 mg/L values, a source and measurement-convention signal rather than gentamicin biology; lineage-grouped CV does not prevent this because a source spans many lineages. The pre-registered credit rule stands (condition 1 was met; condition 2, the single-laboratory external evaluation, decides), and this diagnosis is reported with it.

Bounded-optimiser rerun 65006995 COMPLETE (7h04m, zero RuntimeWarnings, checksums verified). Source-robustness analysis (MIC_EVALUATION_SPEC addendum B) job 65016028 COMPLETE (checksums verified): every human-clinical gentamicin Evo 2 gain vanishes when PRJNA1297298 is excluded (ridge AMR+Evo 2 minus AMR +0.027 to -0.001 [-0.006, +0.002]; XGBoost +0.024 to -0.002 [-0.008, +0.002]; acquired-unit ridge +0.031 to +0.000 [-0.003, +0.002]; acquired-unit XGBoost +0.024 to -0.001) and persists when any other major source is excluded. AMRFinderPlus models versus the no-genome constant remain positive with intervals excluding zero when each major source is excluded, for all drugs in all sources and for ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin in human clinical. All-sources Evo 2 ciprofloxacin ridge gain is small but source-stable (+0.011; +0.007 to +0.015 across exclusions) and is a sensitivity result that cannot create credit; XGBoost Evo 2 lowers ceftriaxone in every exclusion. Limitation found: one BioProject, PRJNA809394 (Walter Reed Army Institute of Research, genomic surveillance at one large US tertiary-care hospital, 2,076 isolates), supplies 73 percent (ceftriaxone), 54 percent (ciprofloxacin) and 62 percent (gentamicin) of human-clinical development rows, so the primary development population largely reflects one hospital laboratory; this must be reported and raises the weight of the independent single-laboratory external evaluation.

Decision owner adopted docs/EXTERNAL_EVALUATION_PLAN.md on 2026-09-29: eight frozen models (no-genome constant, nearest development relative, ridge and XGBoost on AMRFinderPlus, on AMRFinderPlus + Evo 2, and on Evo 2 alone), trained on human-clinical development (primary) and all sources (sensitivity), settings chosen on the five frozen development folds and refitted on all development; one evaluation of the 1,505 external-locked isolates x 3 drugs. Seal protocol implemented and tested: scripts/predict_external.py streams the cohort and reduces external rows to genotype columns on read (tests run every model with unparseable sentinels in the external MIC columns); prediction files carry no reference columns; scripts/attach_external_references.py joins references only to files whose SHA-256 matches the committed config/external_prediction_lock.tsv; hpc/unity/external-evaluate.sbatch runs only against that lock. External prediction array 65019273 submitted. 399 local tests pass, Unity synced identically. No external MIC value, comparator or derived statistic has been read.

LOCK (seal step 2), 2026-09-29, before any external MIC value, comparator or derived statistic was read. External prediction array 65019273 COMPLETE (8 tasks, 30 s to 2h52m; predict_external.py sha256 52e3b356...). Verification read prediction files only: all 16 have 4,515 rows (1,505 isolates x 3 drugs), unique isolate-drug keys, finite predictions, only external rows, no reference columns; every manifest records external_reference_columns_read false; zero RuntimeWarnings; ridge fits not formally converged: 7 (AMR+Evo 2 human clinical), 16 (AMR+Evo 2 all sources), 3 (Evo 2 all sources). The 16 SHA-256 values are committed in config/external_prediction_lock.tsv (sha256 of the lock file recorded in this commit's tree), e.g. ridge AMR human clinical 4940d57d..., ridge AMR+Evo 2 human clinical d828fa8f..., XGBoost AMR human clinical e9d8598f..., XGBoost AMR+Evo 2 human clinical 73364bda..., constant human clinical 703c7ba1..., neighbor human clinical eec69e7c.... Scoring (seal step 3) may use only these files.

External scoring attempt 65020797 (after the lock) FAILED in 9 s with a software defect and produced no metric: the evaluator refused the first baseline file because point-prediction models emit an entirely empty predicted_log2_sd column, which it treated as invalid. References had been joined for that one file (seal step 3, permitted after the lock); no evaluation statistic was computed or read. Fixed in evaluate_mic_predictions.py (an entirely empty sd column means no predictive distribution; a partially empty column is still refused) with a regression test; 400 local tests pass. Per the plan, the rerun uses the same locked prediction files, re-verified against config/external_prediction_lock.tsv, and this failed attempt is reported.

LOCKED EXTERNAL EVALUATION COMPLETE (scoring job 65020832 on predictions 65019273 locked at commit 4c18aa3; checksums verified; earlier attempt 65020797 stopped on a defect before any statistic and is reported). Full results in docs/EXTERNAL_RESULTS.md. Pre-registered: Evo 2 credit NOT awarded for any drug; gentamicin condition 2 failed (AMR+Evo 2 minus AMR, ridge -0.033 [-0.056, -0.015], XGBoost -0.021 [-0.046, +0.000]); ceftriaxone +0.005/+0.015 and ciprofloxacin -0.023/+0.002 not demonstrated; Evo 2 alone worse than AMR for every drug and learner. Human-clinical-trained AMRFinderPlus models, external EA: ciprofloxacin ridge 0.932 [0.894, 0.950], XGBoost 0.933 [0.913, 0.954], resistant under-call 0.012 and 0.025; gentamicin 0.887 [0.841, 0.916] and 0.876 [0.829, 0.909], under-call 0.057 and 0.121; ceftriaxone 0.680 [0.539, 0.742] and 0.597 [0.480, 0.692], under-call 0.258 and 0.513 (pre-declared underpowered); every AMR model beats the no-genome constant with intervals excluding zero. Post-scoring diagnosis: of 710 external ceftriaxone '>64' isolates, 119 were predicted susceptible by ridge AMR; all carried beta-lactamases, led by blaCTX-M-2 (42; 0 in human-clinical development), blaCTX-M-8 (21; 2), blaCTX-M-3 (14; 2), CTX-M-24, CTX-M-65 and blaIMP-1 (0), geographic ESBL variants absent from US/UK-dominated development; plus a reporting-scale effect ('>64' versus development '>=64'). Exploratory, post hoc: among 102 highly resistant carriers of unseen variants, the share predicted resistant was 0.147 (ridge AMR), 0.127 (XGBoost AMR), 0.196 and 0.461 (AMR+Evo 2), 0.784 and 0.814 (Evo 2 alone), against >= 0.98 for common-variant carriers with AMR models: Evo 2 representations generalised to unseen resistance-gene variants where allele-level catalogue features failed; untested against gene-family-pooled catalogue features; hypothesis-generating only.

Post-hoc family analysis (docs/POSTHOC_FAMILY_ANALYSIS.md, specified before its predictions): allele-level AMRFinderPlus symbols plus curated gene-family and AMRFinderPlus subclass indicators, trained on human-clinical development only (job 65022960), external predictions locked at commit ac3a270 before scoring (job 65023163, checksums verified). Primary read-out: of 102 external ceftriaxone >64 mg/L isolates carrying variants absent from development, 0.990 were placed on the resistant side by both family-level learners, against 0.127 to 0.147 for allele-level and 0.784 to 0.814 for Evo 2 alone; the Evo 2 advantage on these isolates is attributable to grouping that curated knowledge supplies more completely. Secondary: family XGBoost external EA ceftriaxone 0.854 [0.784, 0.892] (+0.257 [+0.138, +0.346] over allele-level), ciprofloxacin 0.938 (+0.005), gentamicin 0.901 (+0.025 [+0.014, +0.048]); resistant under-call 10.6, 2.2 and 1.8 percent; family ridge ceftriaxone 0.771 (+0.092 [+0.034, +0.145]). Development nested CV unchanged or higher (XGBoost 0.933, 0.917, 0.895). Post hoc and hypothesis-generating; the family-level catalogue model is the leading candidate for a pre-registered test on a new independent external set.

Search for an independent pre-registrable validation set (metadata and genotype only; no MIC value or phenotype read). Source: EMBL-EBI AMR portal (CABBAGE) release 2026-07, phenotype.csv.gz md5 eb5dd6fcd7c240212b28b257fa112511 (sha256 e6f4f77b...), genotype.csv.gz md5 9309bb9c9208413f20ec226f569cc673, both matching the published md5sums. E. coli: 23,671 isolates across PATRIC, NCBI antibiogram/NDARO, literature curation (CABBAGE_PubMed_data), NARMS, COMPARE_ML, CDC. Excluding NCBI antibiogram/NDARO sources and the 13,493 cohort BioSamples, 3,217 isolates have mg/L measurements for ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin or gentamicin and a run or assembly accession, fragmented across sources (largest: PMID 34485958, UK, 1,092 isolates; Denmark PMID 35756053, 171 with all three drugs; GEMS PMID 30127495, about 184 across seven African and South Asian countries, 2007-2010; Canada PMID 36165686, 123). Using the portal's AMRFinderPlus genotypes, only 21 candidate isolates carry a cephalosporinase or carbapenemase allele rare (fewer than 5) or absent in development (blaNDM-9 7, blaCTX-M-24 4, others 1 to 2), against 102 highly resistant unseen-variant carriers in the JARBS evaluation. Conclusion: current public data do not contain an independent set able to test the family-level hypothesis with useful precision.

Leave-one-variant-out experiment adopted before any run (docs/LEAVE_VARIANT_OUT_PLAN.md, commit ebc0631): human-clinical development ceftriaxone (2,822 isolates); targets by rule, cephalosporinase alleles (intrinsic blaEC excluded) with at least 30 carriers: blaCTX-M-15 410, blaCTX-M-27 170, blaCTX-M-14 47, blaCTX-M-55 39 (primary), blaCMY-2 78 (control: no other CMY allele with 5 or more carriers), blaOXA-1 218 (descriptive); every carrier held out, ridge and XGBoost fitted on allele, family, Evo 2 and AMR+Evo 2 features with settings chosen on the frozen folds restricted to training rows; pre-stated H1 (pooled family minus Evo 2-alone resistant-side share, 95 percent lower bound above -0.05, both learners) and H2 (family minus allele, lower bound above 0). Code and tests in scripts/leave_variant_out.py (synthetic test: held-out allele never trains; family recovers it at over 90 percent where allele-level stays under 20 percent); 405 local tests pass. Array 65051616 (6 targets) and read-out 65051617 submitted. Development only.

Leave-one-variant-out experiment COMPLETE (array 65051616, zero RuntimeWarnings; read-out 65054505, checksums verified; first read-out 65051617 stopped on a software defect, isolates carrying two targets scored once per target, fixed with a regression test, predictions unchanged). Pre-stated hypotheses, pooled over four held-out CTX-M alleles (568 carriers above the panel): H1 family minus Evo 2-alone resistant-side share ridge +0.046 [+0.023, +0.121], XGBoost +0.111 [+0.074, +0.221], supported (family better, not only non-inferior); H2 family minus allele ridge +0.915 [+0.836, +0.943], XGBoost +0.963 [+0.916, +0.981], supported. Per target, allele-level detection 0.022 to 0.111, family 0.972 to 1.000, Evo 2 alone 0.859 to 1.000, AMR+Evo 2 0.189 to 0.861. CMY-2 control (no family relative in training): family 0.773/0.727 via the drug-class indicator, Evo 2 alone 0.227/0.591, allele 0.182. Essential agreement on held-out CTX-M carriers: family 0.74 to 0.95, Evo 2 alone 0.44 to 0.87, allele 0.00 to 0.08. Findings: Evo 2 embeddings alone generalise to unseen CTX-M alleles (confirming the exploratory external direction), curated family and drug-class annotation generalises further and is more MIC-accurate, and combining allele-level catalogue features with Evo 2 loses most of Evo 2's generalisation. Details in docs/LEAVE_VARIANT_OUT_PLAN.md.
